review_notes: I read the whole file and related lines in context. I looked for proof blocks repeated across declarations, mainly in the SizeArch, SizeFinite, Diagonal, BoxMeasure and Exchange sections. I did not search other files for further uses of these lemmas, because all the declarations involved are private. I could not compile anything, so every replacement below is a sketch whose names come from the file or from standard Mathlib. The repeated-block findings are listed most to least significant. private theorem continuousOn_archRealLift3_torus {y₂ : ℝ} (hy₂ : 0 < y₂) :
    ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => archRealLift3 (diagArray ![t * y₂, y₂, 1])) (Set.Ioi 0) := by
findings.problem: The 30-line proof that t ↦ archRealLift3 (diagArray (…)) is continuous on (0,∞) repeats the 27-line proof of the general lemma continuousOn_archRealLift3_diagArray (1046–1072). Both use the same steps: Units.continuous_iff, identify Units.val with archRealMat3 via coe_archRealLift3, apply continuous_archRealMat3_comp, then the same argument for the inverse via archRealLift3_diagArray_inv. The torus lemma's statement is identical to continuousOn_torus₁ (1074–1078), which is proved in three lines from the general lemma. The torus lemma is never used: the only use is continuousOn_torus₁ at line 1292. The only reason for the duplication is that the general lemma sits in a later section.
findings.proposed_change: Move continuousOn_archRealLift3_diagArray (statement d : ℝ → Fin 3 → ℝ, S : Set ℝ, hd, hne, with its existing proof) into the Diagonal section, after continuous_archRealMat3_comp, and delete continuousOn_archRealLift3_torus. Keep continuousOn_torus₁ and continuousOn_torus₂ as the short corollaries they already are. Proof sketch of the general lemma: restrict to S, use Units.continuous_iff, then show the value matrix and the inverse matrix are archRealMat3 of diagonal arrays whose entries are continuous (the entry is t ↦ d t i or its inverse, else a constant). Both torus uses are already written against it, with the hypotheses hd, hne exactly as in continuousOn_torus₁.
findings.benefit: It removes about 30 lines of unused near-copy proof and leaves one maintained proof of diagonal-path continuity. A change to archRealLift3 or archRealMat3 then needs fixing in one place.

obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hC₃.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hf.continuousOn
  exact (integrable_const M).mono' hf.aestronglyMeasurable (hae.mono fun p hp => hM p hp)
findings.problem: The same argument is written three times: a continuous function is integrable for a finite measure that is almost everywhere supported on a compact set. The steps are to bound f on the compact set by exists_bound_of_continuousOn, then use integrable_const M together with Integrable.mono' and the ae-membership. This appears in integrable_of_continuous_boxMeasure (957–961), integrable_of_continuous_boxMeasure₃ (963–968) and integrable_of_continuous_boxMeasure₂ (970–978). In addition, the proof that boxMeasure.prod boxMeasure is ae-supported in C ×ˢ C (h2) is duplicated verbatim in exists_isCompact_ae_mem_boxMeasure₃ (952–953) and integrable_of_continuous_boxMeasure₂ (975–976).
findings.proposed_change: Add one generic lemma: theorem integrable_of_continuous_of_ae_mem {X} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {C : Set X} (hC : IsCompact C) (hae : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ C) {f : X → ℂ} (hf : Continuous f) : Integrable f μ. The proof is the three lines already present: obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hC.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hf.continuousOn; exact (integrable_const M).mono' hf.aestronglyMeasurable (hae.mono fun x hx => hM x hx). Add a second small lemma, ae_mem_prod_of_ae_mem (hC : IsCompact C) (hae : ∀ᵐ x ∂boxMeasure, x ∈ C) : ∀ᵐ q ∂boxMeasure.prod boxMeasure, q ∈ C ×ˢ C, containing the h2 block. Then integrable_of_continuous_boxMeasure is the generic lemma applied to exists_isCompact_ae_mem_boxMeasure. The ₃ version is the generic lemma applied to exists_isCompact_ae_mem_boxMeasure₃. The ₂ version uses the generic lemma with hC.prod hC and ae_mem_prod_of_ae_mem. exists_isCompact_ae_mem_boxMeasure₃ reuses ae_mem_prod_of_ae_mem for h2. The generic lemma needs BorelSpace/measurability of X only through aestronglyMeasurable of a continuous function. That is available here from the local adeleBorel/BorelSpace instances, and the products inherit them. The generic lemma must be stated in the BoxMeasure section so those instances are in scope. Alternatively it can take [OpensMeasurableSpace X] and [SecondCountableTopology X] where needed.
findings.benefit: Each of the three integrability lemmas becomes a one-line application, and the product-support argument is stated once. The key analytic fact (bounded on a compact set, ae in it, so integrable) becomes a named, reusable lemma instead of being re-derived for each product arity.

findings.problem: Three theorems repeat the same skeleton. Each one unfolds matrixSupSize with a long `change Finset.univ.sup …`. It then applies Finset.sup_le and max_le. It then rewrites the coercions of the product and of its inverse to matrix products (the inverse reversed), and finishes with nnnorm_mul_entry_le. The only differences are the entry bounds fed to nnnorm_mul_entry_le (and simpa for a*1 and 1*a). The two matrix-product identities are restated six times, and the long `change` block three times.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one lemma: matrixSupSize_le_of_entries (k : GL (Fin 3) L) {c : NNReal} (h : ∀ i j, ‖(k : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) L) i j‖₊ ≤ c) (h' : ∀ i j, ‖((k⁻¹ : GL (Fin 3) L) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) L) i j‖₊ ≤ c) : matrixSupSize k ≤ c, proved by the single `change … ; exact Finset.sup_le fun ij _ => max_le (h _ _) (h' _ _)`. It needs no ultrametric hypothesis, so mark it with `omit [IsUltrametricDist L] in`, as done for nnnorm_entry_le_matrixSupSize. A second lemma, matrixSupSize_mul_le_of_entries (g k) (a b c) with hypotheses on g, g⁻¹, k, k⁻¹ entries and a*b ≤ c, applies nnnorm_mul_entry_le to both (g*k) and (k⁻¹*g⁻¹). With it: matrixSupSize_mul_le takes a = b-wise matrixSupSize g, matrixSupSize k (and one mul_comm for the inverse side). The `…_le_of_forall_nnnorm_le_one` variants take 1 for the k bounds and use mul_one. The one_mul variant is the same with the roles of g and k swapped. Only the two bound hypotheses differ per use.
findings.benefit: The three 15-line proofs shrink to a few lines each. The entry-wise reduction from the sup-norm to the two entry families is stated once, and the order-reversal of the inverse of a product is handled in one place. This makes the later changes to matrixSupSize's definition cheaper.

findings.problem: The two theorems share their first two `have`s, hrow and hall, character for character. Both apply Finset.single_le_sum twice, first over columns and then over rows, to bound the pair ‖k i j‖ + ‖k⁻¹ i j‖ by matrixSize k. They differ only in the final `linarith` step, which drops one non-negative summand.
findings.proposed_change: Extract norm_entry_add_norm_inv_entry_le_matrixSize (k : GL (Fin 3) L) (i j : Fin 3) : ‖(k : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) L) i j‖ + ‖((k⁻¹ : GL (Fin 3) L) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) L) i j‖ ≤ matrixSize k, with the current hrow/hall proof ending in `hrow.trans hall`. Then norm_entry_le_matrixSize is `by have := norm_entry_add_norm_inv_entry_le_matrixSize k i j; have := norm_nonneg (…inverse entry…); linarith`. The inverse-entry version uses the nonnegativity of the k entry instead.
findings.benefit: It removes about 18 duplicated lines of nested single_le_sum reasoning. The meaningful fact (the pair of entries is bounded by matrixSize) gets a name and one proof.
